# package iec103

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103"
```

Package iec103 implements the application layer of IEC 60870-5-103, the companion standard for the informative interface of protection equipment: its own ASDU model (clause 7.1 to 7.3), the information elements of clause 7.2.6, the function type and information number semantics of clause 7.2.5 as data, and what the controlling and the controlled station share ([State](#type-state), the sentinel errors).

IEC 60870-5-103 does not use the telecontrol ASDU of IEC 60870-5-101 and -104 (package asdu): every field of the data unit identifier is one octet, and the information object is addressed by a function type (FUN) and an information number (INF) instead of an information object address (clause 7.1, figure 2):

	type identification | variable structure qualifier | cause of transmission | common address
	function type | information number | information elements ... | [CP32Time2a]

Every type identification of the compatible range (clause 7.2.1, tables 3 and 4) has a [Body](#type-body) of its own: [TimeTagged](#type-timetagged) (1), [RelTimeTagged](#type-reltimetagged) (2), [Measurands](#type-measurands) (3 and 9), [RelTimeMeasurand](#type-reltimemeasurand) (4), [Identification](#type-identification) (5), [TimeSync](#type-timesync) (6), [GIInit](#type-giinit) (7), [GITermination](#type-gitermination) (8), [GenericData](#type-genericdata) (10), [GenericIdent](#type-genericident) (11), [GeneralCommand](#type-generalcommand) (20), [GenericCommand](#type-genericcommand) (21), [DisturbanceList](#type-disturbancelist) (23), [DisturbanceOrder](#type-disturbanceorder) (24 and 25), [DisturbanceReady](#type-disturbanceready) (26), [ChannelReady](#type-channelready) (27), [TagsReady](#type-tagsready) (28), [Tags](#type-tags) (29), [DisturbanceValues](#type-disturbancevalues) (30) and [EndOfTransmission](#type-endoftransmission) (31). A type identification of the private range (32..255), a reserved one, or a private cause of transmission (64..255; clause 7.2, note: "other combinations may be used in the private range") decodes as [Raw](#type-raw), which keeps every octet: such an ASDU encodes back exactly as it was received.

The serial transport is FT 1.2 (package ft12, clause 6.1) and the unbalanced link procedures of IEC 60870-5-2 (package link, clause 6.2), with a one-octet link address and function code 7 "reset FCB" (clause 6.3). Applications use [github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103/client](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103/client) (the controlling system) and [github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103/server](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103/server) (the protection equipment).

Clause numbers in this package refer to IEC 60870-5-103:1997, read in its identical Russian adoption GOST R IEC 60870-5-103-2005, which keeps the IEC numbering.

```go
	MaxMeasurands2 = 9 // ASDU 9: up to nine MEA (clause 7.3.1.8)
```

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrClosed reports an operation on a closed client or server.
	ErrClosed = errors.New("iec103: closed")
	// ErrLinkDown reports an operation while the link is not initialized
	// (not yet, or no longer after the protection equipment stopped
	// answering).
	ErrLinkDown = errors.New("iec103: link not initialized")
	// ErrInvalidConfig reports a configuration a client or server cannot
	// be built with.
	ErrInvalidConfig = errors.New("iec103: invalid configuration")
	// ErrBusy reports a request while another of the same kind is pending:
	// clause 7.4.4 allows one command procedure at a time, clause 7.4.8.4
	// one generic read and one generic write, clause 7.4.7 one disturbance
	// data transfer.
	ErrBusy = errors.New("iec103: request of the same kind pending")
	// ErrNegative reports a negative answer: a negative acknowledgement of
	// a command (cause 21), of a generic write (cause 41), or a negative
	// end of a disturbance data transfer.
	ErrNegative = errors.New("iec103: negative answer")
	// ErrAborted reports a disturbance data transfer the protection
	// equipment aborted (clause 7.4.7, TOO 34, 37 or 40).
	ErrAborted = errors.New("iec103: transfer aborted by the protection equipment")
	// ErrInHandler reports a client request called on one of the client's
	// own goroutines, from its Handler or OnState, where the answer it
	// waits for cannot arrive: the link loop waits for that goroutine. The
	// request is not sent.
	ErrInHandler = errors.New("iec103: request from inside a handler")
	// ErrResultLimit reports a request whose answer has more ASDUs than
	// the client's Config.MaxResult allows: the request ends there, with
	// the answers so far.
	ErrResultLimit = errors.New("iec103: result limit reached")
	// ErrOverflow reports a request that missed answers: they arrived
	// faster than the request took them, beyond the 1024 ASDUs a request
	// buffers.
	ErrOverflow = errors.New("iec103: answers arrived faster than they were taken")
)
```

Sentinel errors of the controlling and the controlled station; test with errors.Is.

```go
	// type identification.
	ErrTrailing = errors.New("iec103: octets after the information object")
	// ErrInvalid reports a field out of the range the standard defines,
	// for example more elements than an ASDU may carry, or generic data
	// whose length does not match its descriptor.
	ErrInvalid = errors.New("iec103: invalid field")
	// ErrTooLong reports an ASDU that does not fit one FT 1.2 frame.
	ErrTooLong = errors.New("iec103: ASDU too long")
```

## Functions

### func CommandAllowed

```go
func CommandAllowed(fun FunctionType, inf InfoNumber, dco DPI) bool
```

CommandAllowed reports whether a general command (ASDU 20) with double command dco may be sent with (fun, inf): DCO is OFF or ON (clause 7.2.6.4: 0 and 3 are not used), and for a compatible function type INF is one of table 17 (16 to 19, 23 to 26: clause 7.2.5.2 leaves no other information number of the control direction usable with ASDU 20) and the COM column allows only ON for INF 19 (LED reset) and 23 to 26 (activate characteristic 1 to 4). The FUN column of table 17 is typical, not mandatory, so any compatible function type may carry these INF.

## Types

### type ASDU

```go
type ASDU struct {
	// Type is the type identification. Encode takes it from the Body,
	// except for a [Raw] body.
	Type TypeID
	// VSQ is the variable structure qualifier as received. Encode writes
	// the qualifier the Body defines (the number of its elements), except
	// for a [Raw] body.
	VSQ VSQ
	// Cause is the cause of transmission.
	Cause Cause
	// CommonAddr is the common address of ASDU (clause 7.2.4), normally
	// the link address of the protection equipment; 255 is global.
	CommonAddr uint8
	// Fun and Inf are the information object identifier (clause 7.2.5).
	// ASDUs 23 to 31 do not use the information number (it is "not used",
	// clause 7.3.1.11 ff.); it is kept as received and written as given.
	Fun FunctionType
	Inf InfoNumber
	// Body holds the information elements.
	Body Body
}
```

ASDU is an application service data unit of IEC 60870-5-103 (clause 7.1): the data unit identifier, the information object identifier and one information object, the [Body](#type-body).

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte) (*ASDU, error)
```

Decode decodes an ASDU with time tags in UTC.

#### func DecodeIn

```go
func DecodeIn(b []byte, loc *time.Location) (*ASDU, error)
```

DecodeIn decodes an ASDU with time tags in loc (nil means UTC). A type identification outside tables 3 and 4, or a cause of transmission of the private range, gives a [Raw](#type-raw) body; see [DecodeTyped](#func-decodetyped) to interpret a private cause with the compatible structure.

#### func DecodeTyped

```go
func DecodeTyped(b []byte, loc *time.Location) (*ASDU, error)
```

DecodeTyped decodes like [DecodeIn](#func-decodein) but interprets a type identification of tables 3 and 4 with its compatible structure whatever the cause of transmission, for stations whose private causes keep that structure.

#### func New

```go
func New(cause Cause, ca uint8, fun FunctionType, inf InfoNumber, body Body) *ASDU
```

New returns an ASDU with Type and VSQ taken from body.

#### func (ASDU) AppendIn

```go
func (a *ASDU) AppendIn(b []byte, loc *time.Location) ([]byte, error)
```

AppendIn appends the octets of a to b, with time tags in loc (nil means UTC). It fails with ErrTooLong for an ASDU longer than MaxSize.

#### func (ASDU) Encode

```go
func (a *ASDU) Encode() ([]byte, error)
```

Encode returns the octets of a, with time tags in UTC.

#### func (ASDU) String

```go

```

String describes the ASDU, for example "\<1> time-tagged message \<1> spontaneous CA=3 FUN=128 INF=16".

Body is the information elements of an ASDU after the information object identifier. The concrete types are listed in the package documentation; [Raw](#type-raw) holds any other.

### type Catalog

```go
type Catalog struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Catalog maps function type and information number to their semantics. It holds the standard tables and the entries an application adds for private function types or information numbers. A Catalog is safe for concurrent use; the zero value holds the standard tables only.

#### func (Catalog) Add

```go
func (c *Catalog) Add(dir Direction, fun FunctionType, spec InfoSpec)
```

Add records spec for function type fun in direction dir, for every type identification of spec.Types (any type when empty). It takes precedence over the standard tables.

#### func (Catalog) Lookup

```go
func (c *Catalog) Lookup(dir Direction, typ TypeID, fun FunctionType, inf InfoNumber) (InfoSpec, bool)
```

Lookup returns the semantics of (fun, inf) in an ASDU of type typ: an entry added with [Catalog.Add](#func-catalog-add), else, for a function type of a compatible range, the matching entry of tables 8 to 18. A private function type has no standard semantics.

### type Cause

```go
type Cause uint8
```

Cause is the cause of transmission, the third octet of the data unit identifier (clause 7.2.3).

```go
const (
	CauseSpontaneous        Cause = 1  // spontaneous
	CauseCyclic             Cause = 2  // cyclic
	CauseResetFCB           Cause = 3  // reset frame count bit (FCB)
	CauseResetCU            Cause = 4  // reset communication unit (CU)
	CauseStartRestart       Cause = 5  // start / restart
	CausePowerOn            Cause = 6  // power on
	CauseTestMode           Cause = 7  // test mode
	CauseTimeSync           Cause = 8  // time synchronization (both directions)
	CauseGI                 Cause = 9  // general interrogation (both directions: initiation in control direction)
	CauseGITermination      Cause = 10 // termination of general interrogation
	CauseLocalOperation     Cause = 11 // local operation
	CauseRemoteOperation    Cause = 12 // remote operation
	CauseCommandAck         Cause = 20 // positive acknowledgement of command; control direction: general command
	CauseCommandNack        Cause = 21 // negative acknowledgement of command
	CauseDisturbanceData    Cause = 31 // transmission of disturbance data (both directions)
	CauseGenericWriteAck    Cause = 40 // positive acknowledgement of generic write command; control direction: generic write command
	CauseGenericWriteNack   Cause = 41 // negative acknowledgement of generic write command
	CauseGenericReadValid   Cause = 42 // valid data response to generic read command; control direction: generic read command
	CauseGenericReadInvalid Cause = 43 // invalid data response to generic read command
	CauseGenericWriteConf   Cause = 44 // generic write confirmation
)
```

Causes of transmission, monitor direction (table 5).

### type Counted

```go
type Counted struct {
	Count bool // COUNT, bit 7
	Cont  bool // CONT, bit 8
}
```

Counted is the NGD (clause 7.2.6.30) and NDE (clause 7.2.6.35) octet without its number, which the encoder takes from the number of data sets or description elements: COUNT toggles from one ASDU with the same RII to the next, CONT reports that more ASDUs with the same RII follow.

### type Disturbance

```go
type Disturbance struct {
	Fun FunctionType
	TOV uint8
	FAN uint16
	NOF uint16
	// Interval is INT: the time between two values in µs.
	Interval uint16
	// Start is the time tag of the first value (ASDU 26).
```

### type GDD

```go
type GDD struct {
	Type DataType
	// Size is DATASIZE, 1..255: octets of one element, or bits for
	// [DataBitString].
	Size uint8
	// Number is NUMBER, 1..127: the elements in this ASDU.
	Number uint8
	// Cont is CONT: the data continue in the next ASDU with the same RII.
	Cont bool
}
```

GDD is the generic data description (clause 7.2.6.32): CP24{DATATYPE, DATASIZE, NUMBER, CONT}.

#### func (GDD) DataLen

```go
func (g GDD) DataLen() int
```

DataLen returns the length of the GID the description announces (clause 7.2.6.33: DATASIZE times NUMBER). For a packed bit string DATASIZE counts bits and the elements are packed into octets without gaps (clause 7.2.6.32), so the length is the number of octets the bits fill; that rounding is our reading of the "seven and two elements take two octets" example.

Type returns TypeGeneralCommand.

```go
type GenericCommand struct {
	RII   uint8
	Items []Item
}
```

GenericCommand is ASDU 21, the generic command (clause 7.3.2.5): RII, NOG and the generic identifiers. NOG is len(Items).

```go
func (GenericCommand) Type() TypeID
```

Type returns TypeGenericCommand.

### type GenericData

```go
type GenericData struct {
	RII  uint8
	NGD  Counted
	Sets []DataSet
}
```

GenericData is ASDU 10, generic data (clauses 7.3.1.9 and 7.3.2.3): RII, NGD and the data sets. NGD's number is len(Sets), at most MaxCounted.

#### func PackGenericData

```go
func PackGenericData(rii uint8, sets []DataSet) ([]GenericData, error)
```

PackGenericData splits data sets over as many ASDU 10 bodies with the same RII as they need: each at most MaxCounted sets and MaxSize octets, COUNT toggling from one to the next starting at 0, CONT set on all but the last (clauses 7.2.6.30 and 7.4.8.5, figures 13 to 18). No sets give one body with NGD = 0. A data set that does not fit one ASDU fails with ErrTooLong: splitting one GID over several ASDUs (the CONT bit of GDD) is not supported.

#### func (GenericData) Type

```go
func (GenericData) Type() TypeID
```

Type returns TypeGenericData.

```go
	NDE      Counted
	Elements []DescElement
}
```

GenericIdent is ASDU 11, generic identification (clause 7.3.1.10): RII, GIN, NDE and the description elements of that GIN. NDE's number is len(Elements), 1..MaxCounted (clause 7.2.6.35).

#### func PackGenericIdent

```go
func PackGenericIdent(rii uint8, gin GIN, elems []DescElement) ([]GenericIdent, error)
```

PackGenericIdent splits the description elements of one GIN over as many ASDU 11 bodies as they need, like [PackGenericData](#func-packgenericdata) with NDE (clause 7.2.6.35). NDE counts 1..63 elements, so no elements fail with ErrInvalid.

```go
func (GenericIdent) Type() TypeID
```

### type InfoNumber

```go
type InfoNumber uint8
```

InfoNumber is the information number (INF), the second octet of the information object identifier (clause 7.2.5.2). Its meaning depends on the function type and the direction; see [Catalog](#type-catalog).

```go
const (
	InfGIEnd             InfoNumber = 0   // GLB: end of GI (monitor) / GI initiation (control)
	InfTimeSync          InfoNumber = 0   // GLB: time synchronization
	InfResetFCB          InfoNumber = 2   // reset FCB (ASDU 5, COT 3)
	InfResetCU           InfoNumber = 3   // reset CU (ASDU 5, COT 4)
	InfStartRestart      InfoNumber = 4   // start/restart (ASDU 5, COT 5)
	InfPowerOn           InfoNumber = 5   // power on (ASDU 5, COT 6)
	InfReadHeadings      InfoNumber = 240 // GEN: read headings of all defined groups
	InfReadGroup         InfoNumber = 241 // GEN: read values or attributes of all entries of one group
	InfReadDirectory     InfoNumber = 243 // GEN: read directory of a single entry
	InfReadEntry         InfoNumber = 244 // GEN: read value or attribute of a single entry
	InfGenericGI         InfoNumber = 245 // GEN: general interrogation of generic data / its end
	InfWriteEntry        InfoNumber = 248 // GEN: write entry
	InfWriteConfirm      InfoNumber = 249 // GEN: write entry with confirmation
	InfWriteExecute      InfoNumber = 250 // GEN: write entry with execution
	InfWriteAbort        InfoNumber = 251 // GEN: write entry abort
	InfMeasurandsI       InfoNumber = 144 // measurand I (ASDU 3.1)
	InfMeasurandsIV      InfoNumber = 145 // measurands I, V (ASDU 3.2)
	InfMeasurandsIVPQ    InfoNumber = 146 // measurands I, V, P, Q (ASDU 3.3)
	InfMeasurandsINVEN   InfoNumber = 147 // measurands IN, VEN (ASDU 3.4)
	InfMeasurandsIVPQf   InfoNumber = 148 // measurands IL1,2,3, VL1,2,3, P, Q, f (ASDU 9)
	InfLEDReset          InfoNumber = 19  // LED reset
	InfAutoRecloser      InfoNumber = 16  // auto-recloser active / on/off
	InfGeneralStart      InfoNumber = 84  // general start/pick-up
	InfGeneralTrip       InfoNumber = 68  // general trip
	InfFaultLocation     InfoNumber = 73  // fault location X in ohms (ASDU 4)
	InfProtectionActive  InfoNumber = 18  // protection active / protection on/off
	InfMonitorBlocked    InfoNumber = 20  // monitor direction blocked
	InfTestMode          InfoNumber = 21  // test mode
	InfLocalParameterSet InfoNumber = 22  // local parameter setting
)
```

Information numbers of the system and generic functions.

### type InfoSpec

```go
type InfoSpec struct {
	Inf  InfoNumber
	Name string
	// GI reports information included in the general interrogation.
	GI bool
	// Types and Causes are the type identifications and causes of
	// transmission the table lists for it.
	Types  []TypeID
	Causes []Cause
	// Funs are the function types the table lists. For the system and
	// generic functions (GLB, GEN) they are mandatory; elsewhere they are
	// typical. Empty means "according to the main function" (table 8).
	Funs []FunctionType
}
```

InfoSpec is the semantics of one information number (clause 7.2.5.2, tables 8 to 18).

#### func StandardInfo

```go
func StandardInfo(dir Direction, inf InfoNumber) []InfoSpec
```

StandardInfo returns the entries of tables 8 to 18 for inf in direction dir. Information number 0 has two entries in each direction (general interrogation and time synchronization).

```go
type Item struct {
	GIN GIN

}
```

Item is one generic identifier of a generic command (ASDU 21): GIN and KOD (clause 7.2.6.37).

### type KOD

```go
type KOD uint8
```

KOD is the kind of description (clause 7.2.6.34).

```go
const (
	KODNone           KOD = 0  // no kind of description specified
	KODActualValue    KOD = 1  // actual value
	KODDefaultValue   KOD = 2  // default value
	KODRange          KOD = 3  // range (minimum, maximum, step size)
	KODPrecision      KOD = 5  // precision (n, m)
	KODFactor         KOD = 6  // factor
	KODReference      KOD = 7  // % reference
	KODEnumeration    KOD = 8  // enumeration
	KODDimension      KOD = 9  // dimension
	KODDescription    KOD = 10 // description
	KODPassword       KOD = 12 // password entry
	KODReadOnly       KOD = 13 // read only
	KODWriteOnly      KOD = 14 // write only
	KODFunInf         KOD = 19 // corresponding function type and information number
	KODEvent          KOD = 20 // corresponding event
	KODTextArray      KOD = 21 // enumerated text array
	KODValueArray     KOD = 22 // enumerated value array
	KODRelatedEntries KOD = 23 // related entries
)
```

Kinds of description.

### type MEA

```go
type MEA struct {
	Raw      int16 // MVAL, -4096..4095
	Overflow bool  // OV
	Error    bool  // ER: MVAL is not a valid value
}
```

MEA is a measurand with quality descriptor (clause 7.2.6.8): CP16{OV, ER, RES, MVAL}. MVAL is a 13-bit two's complement fraction F13 in -1..+1-2^-12, held here as the integer Raw in -4096..4095 (the value is Raw/4096). Full scale (the largest MVAL) stands for 1.2 or 2.4 times the rated value, so the rated value is Raw 3413 or 1707. A Raw outside -4096..4095 does not fit MVAL: an ASDU that carries it does not encode (ErrInvalid).

#### func MEAOf

```go
func MEAOf(v float64) MEA
```

MEAOf returns the measurand for v (clamped to the range of MVAL; a value outside it sets OV, as clause 7.2.6.8 requires on overflow).

#### func (MEA) Value

```go
func (m MEA) Value() float64
```

Value returns MVAL as a fraction of the full scale.

### type Measurands

```go
type Measurands struct {
	Set2   bool
	Values []MEA
}
```

Measurands is ASDU 3 (measurands I, clause 7.3.1.3; Set2 false) or ASDU 9 (measurands II, clause 7.3.1.8; Set2 true). The meaning of the values depends on the information number (table 14); ASDU 9 always starts with IL1, so fewer values leave out the last ones.

#### func (Measurands) Type

```go
func (m Measurands) Type() TypeID
```

Type returns TypeMeasurands1 or TypeMeasurands2.

### type Raw

```go
type Raw struct{ Data []byte }
```

Raw is a body this package does not interpret: a type identification of the private or reserved range, or a private cause of transmission. Data holds every octet after the information number; with the Type and VSQ of the ASDU it encodes back exactly as received.

#### func (Raw) Type

```go
func (Raw) Type() TypeID
```

Type returns 0: the type identification of a raw body is the ASDU's.

### type SOF

```go
type SOF uint8
```

SOF is the status of fault (clause 7.2.6.24).

```go
const (
	SOFTrip SOF = 0x01 // TP: recorded fault with trip
	SOFTM   SOF = 0x02 // TM: disturbance data being transmitted
	SOFTest SOF = 0x04 // TEST: recorded during test mode
	SOFOTEV SOF = 0x08 // OTEV: recording initiated by another event than start/pick-up
)
```

Bits of SOF.

### type State

```go
type State uint8
```

State is the state of the link as seen by one station.

```go
const (
	// StateDown: the link is not initialized.
	StateDown State = iota
	// StateUp: the link is initialized and user data flows.
	StateUp
	// StateClosed: the station was closed.
	StateClosed
)
```

Link states.

#### func (State) String

```go
func (s State) String() string
```

### type TOO

```go
type TOO uint8
```

TOO is the type of order (clause 7.2.6.26).

```go
const (
	TOOSelectFault        TOO = 1  // selection of fault
	TOORequestData        TOO = 2  // request for disturbance data
	TOOAbortData          TOO = 3  // abortion of disturbance data
	TOORequestChannel     TOO = 8  // channel request
	TOOAbortChannel       TOO = 9  // abortion of channel
	TOORequestTags        TOO = 16 // request for tags
	TOOAbortTags          TOO = 17 // abortion of tags
	TOORequestList        TOO = 24 // request for list of recorded disturbances
	TOOEndData            TOO = 32 // end of disturbance data transmission without abortion
	TOOEndDataAbortCtrl   TOO = 33 // end of disturbance data transmission, aborted by the control system
	TOOEndDataAbortProt   TOO = 34 // end of disturbance data transmission, aborted by the protection equipment
	TOOEndChannel         TOO = 35 // end of channel transmission without abortion
	TOOEndChannelAbortCtl TOO = 36 // end of channel transmission, aborted by the control system
	TOOEndChannelAbortPrt TOO = 37 // end of channel transmission, aborted by the protection equipment
	TOOEndTags            TOO = 38 // end of tag transmission without abortion
	TOOEndTagsAbortCtrl   TOO = 39 // end of tag transmission, aborted by the control system
	TOOEndTagsAbortProt   TOO = 40 // end of tag transmission, aborted by the protection equipment
	TOODataOK             TOO = 64 // disturbance data transmitted successfully (positive)
	TOODataFailed         TOO = 65 // disturbance data transmitted not successfully (negative)
	TOOChannelOK          TOO = 66 // channel transmission successful (positive)
	TOOChannelFailed      TOO = 67 // channel transmission not successful (negative)
	TOOTagsOK             TOO = 68 // tags transmitted successfully (positive)
	TOOTagsFailed         TOO = 69 // tags transmitted not successfully (negative)
)
```

Types of order. 1..31 go with ASDU 24, 32..63 with ASDU 31, 64..95 with ASDU 25 (clause 7.2.6.26).

### type TypeID

```go
type TypeID uint8
```

TypeID is the type identification, the first octet of the data unit identifier (clause 7.2.1).

```go
const (
	TypeTimeTagged        TypeID = 1  // time-tagged message
	TypeRelTimeTagged     TypeID = 2  // time-tagged message with relative time
	TypeMeasurands1       TypeID = 3  // measurands I
	TypeRelTimeMeasurand  TypeID = 4  // time-tagged measurands with relative time
	TypeIdentification    TypeID = 5  // identification
	TypeTimeSync          TypeID = 6  // time synchronization
	TypeGIInit            TypeID = 7  // general interrogation (control direction)
	TypeGITermination     TypeID = 8  // general interrogation termination
	TypeMeasurands2       TypeID = 9  // measurands II
	TypeGenericData       TypeID = 10 // generic data
	TypeGenericIdent      TypeID = 11 // generic identification
	TypeGeneralCommand    TypeID = 20 // general command (control direction)
	TypeGenericCommand    TypeID = 21 // generic command (control direction)
	TypeDisturbanceList   TypeID = 23 // list of recorded disturbances
	TypeDisturbanceOrder  TypeID = 24 // order for disturbance data transmission (control direction)
	TypeDisturbanceAck    TypeID = 25 // acknowledgement for disturbance data transmission (control direction)
	TypeDisturbanceReady  TypeID = 26 // ready for transmission of disturbance data
	TypeChannelReady      TypeID = 27 // ready for transmission of a channel
	TypeTagsReady         TypeID = 28 // ready for transmission of tags
	TypeTags              TypeID = 29 // transmission of tags
	TypeDisturbanceValues TypeID = 30 // transmission of disturbance values
	TypeEndOfTransmission TypeID = 31 // end of transmission
)
```

Type identifications of the compatible range (clause 7.2.1, tables 3 and 4). Types 6 and 10 exist in both directions with the same structure.

#### func (TypeID) Compatible

```go
func (t TypeID) Compatible() bool
```

Compatible reports a type identification of the compatible range 1..31 (clause 7.2.1). Values of that range that tables 3 and 4 do not define are reserved; [TypeID.Defined](#func-typeid-defined) tells them apart.

#### func (TypeID) Defined

```go
func (t TypeID) Defined() bool
```

Defined reports a type identification tables 3 or 4 define.

#### func (TypeID) String

```go
func (t TypeID) String() string
```

String returns the name of the type identification, for example "\<1> time-tagged message", or "\<200> private".

VSQ is the variable structure qualifier (clause 7.2.2): the number of information elements in bits 1..7 and SQ in bit 8.
